papers.title: Development of non-toxic low-cost bioactive porous Ti–Fe–Si bulk metallic glass with bone-like mechanical properties for orthopedic implants
papers.abstract: The clinical value of large-sized Ti-based bulk metallic glass (BMG) used in orthopedic implants has greatly diminished because of the internal toxic/precious elements and the aseptic loosening caused by not only the “stress shielding” effect, but also the biological inertia of the alloy surface. Here, a toxic elements-free low-cost Ti–Fe–Si porous BMG with bone-like compressive strength (130 MPa) and Young's modulus (37 GPa) was fabricated by mechanical alloying (MA) and bonded with spark plasma sintering (SPS). By altering the loading pressure during the SPS process, the porosity and mechanical properties of the Ti–Fe–Si BMG can be effectively regulated to meet the requirements of the load-bearing cortical bone. Moreover, in vitro biological experiments revealed that the Ti–Fe–Si BMG possesses favorable bioactivity to induce the apatite and excellent biocompatibility for cell proliferation, similar to that of commercial pure Ti (cp-Ti). State-of-art Ti–Fe–Si porous BMG with global bone-like properties can be expected to be an important biomaterial for clinical orthopedic use.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文开发了一种新型多孔钛基金属玻璃，虽然提及应力遮挡，但没有进行任何股骨植入物的有限元分析或界面力学建模。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on material synthesis and characterization, but does not include any finite element analysis, implant-bone interface modeling, micromotion quantification, or stress/strain analysis in femoral zones.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发无毒低成本的钛基多孔金属玻璃以减小应力遮挡并提高生物活性
summary_zh.method: 采用机械合金化和放电等离子烧结制备Ti-Fe-Si多孔金属玻璃，通过压力调控孔隙率
summary_zh.result: 获得骨匹配的压缩强度(130MPa)和弹性模量(37GPa)及良好生物活性

summary_en.motivation: To develop a toxic-element-free, low-cost porous Ti-based bulk metallic glass with bone-like mechanical properties to mitigate stress shielding and enhance bioactivity for orthopedic implants.
summary_en.method: The Ti-Fe-Si porous BMG was fabricated via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering, with porosity and mechanical properties controlled by adjusting SPS loading pressure.
summary_en.result: The synthesized BMG exhibited compressive strength (130 MPa) and Young's modulus (37 GPa) matching cortical bone, along with favorable apatite formation and cell proliferation comparable to pure titanium.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing confirmed bone-like compressive properties, and in vitro biological assays demonstrated bioactivity and biocompatibility.
